name: Trowel
description: A small hand shovel with a pointed, dished blade. Good for planting, weeding and digging out small holes.
notes: 250 mm: a 110 mm oak handle, a cranked steel neck and a 75 mm pointed blade dished 12 mm, lying on its back. Brings digging 1 and a little cutting; the reference's negative butchering is left out.

name: Hoe
description: A long-handled garden hoe with a flat steel blade set square to the handle, for chopping weeds and breaking up soil.
notes: 1.4 m: a 1.3 m handle, steel socket and gooseneck, and a 150 by 100 mm blade hanging square to the handle with a bright ground edge. The reference's wood sawing quality is left out: a hoe does not saw. The box counts the air around a long handle and its head, so box/volume runs high; the tool itself is close to the reference volume.

name: Bronze hoe
description: A hand-made hoe with a cast bronze blade. Heavier than a steel one and softer at the edge.
notes: Rides on the hoe model with bronze metal; the reference makes it nearly three times as heavy as the steel hoe (3.1 kg).

name: Wooden shovel
description: A shovel carved from a single piece of hardwood. It moves earth, slowly, and splinters if pushed too hard.
notes: 1.2 m, all oak: an 830 mm round handle with a knob, a flared shoulder and a 200 mm blade dished 30 mm with a rounded tip. The box counts the air around a long handle and its head, so box/volume runs high; the tool itself is close to the reference volume.

name: Garden rake
description: A steel bow rake on a long wooden handle, for levelling soil and dragging out stones and roots.
notes: 1.5 m: a 1.4 m handle, a steel ferrule, two flat bows and a 380 mm head with 14 tines, lying on its back with the tines up, painted green. No crafting quality: raking is not one any recipe asks for. The box counts the air around a long handle and its head, so box/volume runs high; the tool itself is close to the reference volume.

name: Leaf rake
description: A light fan rake with flexible plastic tines. Made for gathering leaves and not much else.
notes: 1.5 m: a 1 m wooden handle in a green plastic collar and a fan of 22 flat tines spreading to 550 mm, two cross braces and upturned tips. No crafting quality. The box counts the air around a long handle and its head, so box/volume runs high; the tool itself is close to the reference volume.

name: Scythe
description: A long curved blade on a two-handled wooden shaft, swung low to mow grass and grain. Clumsy at anything else.
notes: 1.4 m: a wooden snath with two grips and a 700 mm tempered blade curving off the far end, laid flat. Grass cutting is a new quality name for mowing and harvesting. A melee block is left to the content pass. The box counts the air around a long handle and its head, so box/volume runs high; the tool itself is close to the reference volume.

name: Scythe
description: A long curved blade on a two-handled wooden shaft, swung low to mow grass and grain. Clumsy at anything else.
notes: Rides on the scythe model unchanged; the reference makes it a lighter scythe (1.84 kg) with the same name. Whether it needs its own item is for the content pass.

name: Reaper's scythe
description: A costume scythe of hollow plastic, its oversized blade moulded with a grinning skull. Useless for mowing.
notes: 1.4 m: a black plastic pole with two moulded knots and a wide grey blade carrying a raised bone-coloured skull, built on the scythe outline without grips. The skull is small at tile scale. The box counts the air around a long handle and its head, so box/volume runs high; the tool itself is close to the reference volume.

name: Shovel
description: A long-handled round-point shovel. Digs, scoops and makes a heavy, awkward club.
notes: 1.4 m: a 1.08 m wooden handle, a steel socket and a 230 by 290 mm round-point blade dished 35 mm with treads, painted dark. The reference's cooking quality is left out. A melee block is left to the content pass. The box counts the air around a long handle and its head, so box/volume runs high; the tool itself is close to the reference volume.

name: Snow shovel
description: A wide shovel for pushing and lifting snow. It will dig, badly.
notes: Rides on the round-point shovel model with a galvanised blade, as the brief puts variants on their root's model; a real snow shovel has a wide square scoop, so it wants its own row if the content pass keeps it.

name: Plastic snow shovel
description: A light snow shovel with a plastic scoop. It cracks on frozen ground.
notes: Rides on the round-point shovel model with a blue plastic blade; a real snow shovel has a wide square scoop, so it wants its own row if the content pass keeps it.

name: Sickle
description: A short-handled hook of a blade for cutting grass and harvesting grain by hand.
notes: 470 by 340 mm: a 130 mm oak handle, a ferrule and a crescent blade on a 170 mm radius, its edge on the inside. The reference's butchering is left out: a sickle is a harvesting tool. The box counts the air around a long handle and its head, so box/volume runs high; the tool itself is close to the reference volume.

name: Bronze sickle
description: A hand-made sickle with a cast bronze blade.
notes: Rides on the sickle model with bronze metal (1.0 kg).

name: Stone sickle
description: A stick with a knapped crescent of stone lashed along one side. It cuts grass, barely.
notes: 330 mm: a bark-covered haft with a 35 mm wide stone crescent set along its side, bound at both ends with rawhide.

name: Hedge trimmer
description: A petrol hedge trimmer with a long double-sided cutter bar. Loud, heavy and thirsty.
notes: 1 m: a 330 mm orange engine housing with a frosted fuel tank, recoil starter and muffler, a rear loop grip, a front bail and hand guard, and a 530 mm bar with 14 teeth each side. Running it, fuel and its on state are for the content pass. The box counts the air round the handles and bar (box/volume x26.5); the reference's 2.5 L is far below the engine's real bulk.
